author: @FrankCurzio
text:
BREAKING: Drones just set one of Russia's two biggest Baltic oil ports on fire.

Three workers were hurt at Ust-Luga, the regional governor said. The port ships roughly 700,000 barrels of oil a day.

On Monday it was a refinery. Now Ukraine is hitting the place Russia sells its oil from, and that export money pays for the war (right before US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi this week).

Brent fell below $90 on hopes the Iran war ends, and Trump calls Abu Dhabi a chance for a breakthrough. Oil under $90 assumes two wars end at once.

A deal doesn't fix a burned terminal.

Chevron is moving drilling money to places no drone can reach, and services companies like Halliburton get paid to do that work.

I'd rather own the companies drilling far from every war zone.
